# Dimension 1: Platform Overview & Architecture

Reference file for [citations.md](../citations.md).

## What is n8n?

n8n is a visual workflow automation platform with native AI capabilities, built
with TypeScript and Node.js [3]. It combines a drag-and-drop visual interface
with custom code capabilities (JavaScript, Python) [40]. The platform uses a
node-based architecture where workflows are directed graphs of nodes that
receive, transform, and pass data [3].

## Architecture

n8n uses a frontend-backend separated design [3]:

| Layer | Technology | Purpose |
|-------|-----------|---------|
| Client | Browser | User interaction |
| Presentation | Vue 3 + Pinia | Visual editor |
| API | Express.js REST + WebSocket | Communication |
| Business Logic | TypeScript | Core operations |
| Execution | Node.js | Workflow processing |
| Data Access | TypeORM | Database abstraction |
| Node Ecosystem | TypeScript plugins | Integrations |

Workflows are stored as JSON and processed node-by-node, with output from one
node feeding into the next [3].

## Execution Modes

1. **Default mode:** All nodes run in the main process. Concurrency controlled
   via environment variables [3].

2. **Queue mode:** Distributes tasks to multiple workers via Redis using BullMQ.
   Main instance handles UI/API/webhooks; workers pull from Redis and execute
   [3][9][49].

## Licensing

- Originally Apache 2.0 with Commons Clause [1]
- Changed to **Sustainable Use License (SUL)** in March 2022 [1][14]
- Described as "fair-code": source-available, extendable, commercially
  restricted [14]
- **Not** Open Source Initiative (OSI) compliant due to commercial use
  restrictions [14]
- Allows use and modification for internal business or non-commercial purposes [14]

## Core Concepts

| Concept | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Workflows** | Directed graphs of nodes; stored as JSON [3] |
| **Nodes** | Building blocks for loading, processing, and sending data [3] |
| **Triggers** | Starting points: external events or scheduled [3] |
| **Credentials** | Encrypted authentication data for external services (AES256) [33][48] |
| **Expressions** | `{{ }}` syntax for JavaScript expressions accessing workflow data [3] |

## Performance Characteristics

- Resource requirements: 2-core CPU and 4GB RAM for most cases [3]
- ~100MB RAM at idle [43]
- 4GB RAM recommended for 10-20 workflows [43]
- Not suitable for ultra-high-frequency or low-latency scenarios [3]
- Single-process bottleneck under high concurrency in default mode [3]
